# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.

# Repository Exploration Report: /app

## 1. Overall Repo Structure

This is a **Python 3.9 Flask microservice** for Indian bank transaction enrichment/categorization, packaged with setuptools and deployed via Docker/gunicorn. There is **only one top-level project directory**:

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                     # python:3.9.2 base; pip install -e .; gunicorn on port 9898
├── .gitignore                     # note: *.csv is ignored (no data files in repo)
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                   # deps: Flask 1.1.2, pandas, numpy, fuzzywuzzy, python-Levenshtein, sklearn, scipy
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py            # Flask app factory, request timing hooks
        ├── Controller.py          # HTTP routes: /categorizeTransaction, /recurrentTransactions
        ├── BankScripts/           # 35 per-bank rule files (HDFC.py, SBI.py, ICICI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/        # shared regex constants, name cleaning, purpose/PFM logic, enums
```

- **Language:** Python (pandas/numpy vectorized regex rules; no ML models despite sklearn dep)
- **Build tooling:** `pip3 install -e .` from `/app/categorizationapp` (per Dockerfile)
- **Pipeline** (per bank, in `Controller.py`): `categorize_<Bank>_transactions()` → `purpose()` → `clean_names()` → `internal_payment()` → `salary_detection()` → optional `pfm_categorization()` + `simple_description()`

## 2. Transaction Categorization Logic

Categorization is **rule-based (regex over the `description` column)** using `np.select(conditions, choices)` tables, one file per bank:

- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py`** — 35 files, each with `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)`. Example, `HDFC.py`:
  - Cheque: `CHEQUE_PAID` / `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` / `CHEQUE_RETURN` via patterns like `\bCHQ\b`, `Chq Paid|CHQ COLL`, `CHQ DEP RET` (lines 69–75)
  - Electronic transfers: `UPI`, `IMPS`, `NEFT`, `RTGS`, `TPT`, `FUND_TRANSFER` (lines 56–63, 96); default category is `TRANSFER`
  - Account verification: line 13 — `BANK_VER` regex + `amount < 2` → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py`** — bank-specific regex constants, incl. `BANK_VER` / `BANK_VER_HD` (penny-drop/account-verification patterns: "pennydrop", "verif", "/BAV-", "TestVPA", ...), `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10` (MICR clearing cheque parsing), `CHQ_PATTERN1..4` ("MICR INWARD... TO CLG"), `FT_PATTERN*`, `BANK_CHARGES_*`
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py`** — cross-bank merchant/domain regexes (loans, education, IT services, microfinance, ...)
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py`** — canonical category enum (`CHEQUE_PAID`, `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, `NEFT`, `IMPS`, `UPI`, `RTGS`, `TRANSFER`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, reversals, charges, etc.)
- **`TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py`** — subcategories (salary, loan, investment, internal payment, ...)
- Downstream enrichment: `Purpose.py` / `CardPurpose.py` (purpose assignment), `PFMCategorization.py` + `SimpleDescription.py` (PFM categories), `SalaryDetection.py`, `InternalPayment.py` (fuzzy-matches accountHolder), `RecurrentTxns.py`

## 3. Counterparty-Name Extraction (e.g. "CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR")

Name extraction is done **inside each BankScripts file** (they set a `partyName` column), using positional token-split helpers plus regex extraction:

- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py`** — the core parsing primitives: `sep_by_dash(desc, n1, n2)` (split narration on `-` and take token slice), plus `sep_by_` (slash), `sep_by_colon`, `sep_by_comma`, `sep_by_star`, `sep_by_under`, etc., and `py_extract(desc, pat, index)` (regex `str.extract` with NaN handling), `fuzzy_match`
- **Per-bank extraction tables** — e.g. `HDFC.py` lines 146–275: UPI/IMPS/NEFT token positions (`sep_by_dash(description, 2, 3)` for `^IMPS-|^NEFT [CD][Rr]`), and cheque narrations: line 163 handles `CHQ PAID-` via `sep_by_dash(description, 3, 4)`; lines 188–197 apply `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10` (MICR CLG variants). Other examples: `Central.py:73-74` (`CHQ PAID (.*) -`), `Canara.py:165` (`^CHQ PAID-` → token 1), `Axis.py:145` (`BRN-CLG-CHQ PAID TO ...`), `AuSmallFinanceBank.py:78`, `Citi.py:119-143`
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py`** (1971 lines) — `clean_names()`: post-extraction normalization mapping raw partyName strings to canonical merchant names (huge regex → name lookup: DTH, broadband, utilities, banks, ...)
- **`CardCleanNames.py` / `CardPurpose.py`** — same for credit-card transactions
- Relevant regex constant groups for name extraction: `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1-10`, `HDFC_FT_PATTERN1-7`, `FT_PATTERN8-11`, `CHQ_PATTERN1-4`, `HDFC_POS_PATTERN`, `POS_REFUND_PATTERN`, `SI_PATTERN`, `HDFC_CLEAN1` — all in `BankRegexConstants.py`

## 4. Test Fixtures / Baseline Corpus / Test Commands

**There are none in this repository.** I verified thoroughly:

- No `tests/`, `test_*.py`, `conftest.py`, fixture, or baseline files anywhere under `/app` (or elsewhere on the filesystem outside system dirs)
- No pytest/tox/CI config (no `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg` test config, no `.github/`, no Makefile)
- `setup.py` declares no test dependencies; the only git history is a single commit ("import codebase")
- Notably, **`.gitignore` excludes `*.csv`**, so any transaction corpus used for baseline evaluation was deliberately kept out of version control
- The only "test"-related strings in code are comments ("For testing purpose only" in `SalaryDetection.py:27` and `RecurrentTxns.py:16`) and the account-verification regexes themselves (which match narrations containing "testing"/"TestVPA")

**How to run/exercise the code** (the only executable entry points):
```bash
# install
cd /app/categorizationapp && pip3 install -e .

# run the service (as in the Dockerfile)
gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app
# or dev mode: python -m categorizationapp  (Flask on port 9898)

# exercise categorization via HTTP
POST /categorizeTransaction  {"bank": "HDFC", "acc_type": "SAVING", "accountUID": "...", "accountHolder": "...", "transactions": [...]}
POST /recurrentTransactions  {"accountUID": "...", "transactions": [...]}
```

If you plan to add a baseline/fixture test harness, the natural seams are the pure functions `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(df, accountType)` (BankScripts) and `clean_names(df, accountType, bank)` (CleanName.py), which take/return plain pandas DataFrames with `description`, `type`, `amount`, `remark`, `balanceAfterTransaction` columns.
</task_result>
</task>

todos.content: Investigate F-1: bare-digit cheque note miscategorized as TRANSFER (PNB.py:60)
Investigate F-2: CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-<name> returns clearing tag (Canara.py:165)
Investigate F-3: NEFT credits with blank counterparty name (Canara.py:117)
Investigate F-4: IMPS credit shows reference number instead of sender name (Bandhan.py:61)
Investigate F-5: account-verification credit filed as TRANSFER (Canara.py:19)
Fix all confirmed regressions
Verify fixes with reproduction script; ensure no collateral changes

steps.message:
All five findings are root-caused and fixed. Since the repo ships no fixtures or tests, I traced each finding to its rule by cross-checking sibling rules that handle the same narration families, then verified behaviorally with a reproduction harness.

## Root causes and fixes

**F-1 — bare cheque-number note → TRANSFER** — `BankScripts/PNB.py:60`
The debit-side rule matched remarks of exactly 5 digits (`^[0-9]{5}$`) while its credit twin on the next line matches `^[0-9]{5,6}$`. A 6-digit cheque number with nothing else beside it fell through to the `TRANSFER` default. Fixed the debit rule to `^[0-9]{5,6}$`, matching its credit sibling.

**F-2 — `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` returns the clearing tag** — `BankScripts/Canara.py:165`
The rule took dash-token 1 (`MICR CLG`, the internal clearing tag) instead of token 2 (the payee name). The sibling rule directly above (`Chq Paid-Home Clearing-` → token 2) shows the correct index for this narration family. Changed `sep_by_dash(...,1,2)` → `sep_by_dash(...,2,3)`; now yields `Ravi Kumar`.

**F-3 — NEFT credits with blank counterparty** — `BankScripts/Canara.py:117`
The `NEFT-` rule took token 1, which in the `NEFT-<UTR>-<NAME>-<IFSC>` layout is the numeric UTR; a later cleanup (`Canara.py:174`, `^[0-9]{5,}` → `""`) then blanked it, leaving category `NEFT` correct but the name empty. Other layouts (`NEFT CR-`, `NEFT:`) use token 2 and were unaffected. Changed to token 2; name now resolves.

**F-4 — IMPS P2P credit shows the bare reference number** — `BankScripts/Bandhan.py:61`
The generic `IMPS/` rule takes slash-token 2, which for mode-bearing layouts (`IMPS/P2P/<ref>/<name>/...`) is the 12-digit reference; Bandhan has no digit-blanking cleanup, so the number surfaced verbatim. Its UPI siblings (`UPI/[CD]R/[0-9]+/` → token 3) show the correct index for this family. Added a specific rule `IMPS/P2[AP]/[0-9]+/` → token 3 ahead of the generic rule, so the generic rule's behavior for all other IMPS forms (including the 3-token and spaced `I M P S /` layouts) is unchanged.

**F-5 — account-verification credit filed as TRANSFER** — `BankScripts/Canara.py:19`
The gate was `amount.lt(1)`, which excludes the canonical ₹1 penny-drop credit. Every other bank script uses `lt(2)`, `eq(1)` or `isin([1,-1])` (e.g. HDFC.py:13 uses `lt(2)`). Changed to `lt(2)`.

## Verification

- Reproduced all five symptoms exactly as reported before the change, and confirmed each derives the expected value after.
- Ran a 46-row synthetic corpus across the three touched scripts against pre- and post-fix code: the diff contains only rows in the five regressed families; every control row (5-digit cheque notes, credit-side cheque deposits, other NEFT/RTGS/UPI layouts, 3-token and spaced IMPS forms, sub-rupee verifications, ordinary ₹1 deposits, card/cash/auto-pay rows) is byte-identical.
- `compileall` passes on all bank scripts; no other files touched.

One additional anomaly worth flagging to whoever owns the baseline: `BankScripts/RBL.py:137` contains a literal `<<<< INCONSISTENT >>>>` token inside a partyName-cleanup regex — it is inert (can never match a real party name), it does not correspond to any of the five listed findings, and any guessed replacement risked moving currently-correct rows, so I left it untouched.
